common:
**From:** Priya Nandakumar  
**To:** Cody  
**Subject:** RE: Halberd & Vale, LAPTOP-JU4M3I0E

Morning, Cody.

I forwarded your report to Tomás at 06:40. He called me at 06:52, which tells you how it landed.

After reading it, Tomás went and physically checked the laptop. It turns out a contractor had borrowed it the week before to "test a free rendering plugin" they'd found online, and `testme.js` came out of that download. The contractor has been asked some pointed questions, the laptop has been pulled for reimaging, and Halberd & Vale are resetting every credential that was ever typed on it.

Notice what happened there: the logs couldn't tell us how that script arrived, and you were right not to guess. The answer came from a person walking over to a desk, *because* your report told them exactly what to look for.

"Probably a false positive. Nobody did anything unusual." Remember that sentence. You'll hear it again.

by_grade.S: Honestly? That's the cleanest first report I've had from a new hire. Every claim had a record number, you separated what you saw from what you think, and your unknowns list is better than some of my seniors'. I've put it in the team wiki as the example. Don't let it go to your head.
by_grade.A: Strong work. Your core findings were right and properly evidenced. A couple of the subtler details got past you; read the reference write-up and see which ones. That's the difference between good and great in this job, and it's learnable.
by_grade.B: Solid start. You found the important part, but you left points on the table: some of the quieter details in that export matter more than they look. Go through the reference investigation slowly, line by line, against your own notes. Dee says the second case is where it clicks for most people.
by_grade.C: You got the shape of it, but too much of the report rests on things you didn't prove. That's normal on night one. Dee will sit with you tomorrow and walk through the export field by field. Then rerun the case cold. Seriously: reset it and do it again.
by_grade.D: Rough first night, and that's fine. Everyone has one. Before the next shift, reset this case and work it again from the top with the toolkit notes open. Read every field of every event. Don't open a single hint until you've written down what you think it means.

next:
---

**One more thing.** Dee caught me on my way out:

> "That `cmdkey … Microsoft_Windows_Shell_ZipFolder` line you flagged? Ran a hunt across the other clients. Got a hit at **Corvid Logistics** from last week. Same trick, different machine, except on that one *something stayed behind after reboot*. Want to give the new hire a crack at it?"

I told her I'd ask you. Get some sleep first.

— Priya

**Chapter 2: Echoes in the Scheduler** is coming.
